title: Seattle Police Chief Shon Barnes Resigns Over Botched Response to Bite of Seattle Shooting
excerpt: Mayor Katie Wilson names Deputy Chief Andre Sayles as interim replacement after days of criticism over communication failures following the mass shooting that killed three and wounded four.
body:
• Seattle Police Chief Shon Barnes resigned Thursday after Mayor Katie Wilson asked him to step down over the department's widely criticised response to the Bite of Seattle mass shooting.
  • Three people, including one suspected shooter, were killed and four wounded — among them a 2-year-old boy — when gunfire erupted at the annual food festival on July 26.
  • Deputy Chief Andre Sayles, a law-enforcement veteran with more than two decades of experience, has been appointed interim chief.
  • Black community leaders, including the Seattle NAACP, rallied at City Hall to protest what they called a politically motivated ouster.

Seattle Police Chief Shon Barnes tendered his resignation on Thursday after days of mounting criticism over the department's sluggish communication in the wake of a mass shooting at the Bite of Seattle food festival. Mayor Katie Wilson accepted the resignation and immediately named Deputy Chief Andre Sayles as his interim replacement.

The departure caps a turbulent four days that saw Barnes face questions about his absence from the city during the shooting, a confrontational exchange with a reporter, and growing political pressure from the mayor's office.

The Shooting and the Communication Breakdown

Gunfire broke out on the evening of Sunday, July 26, outside the Seattle Center Armory during the Bite of Seattle, an annual three-day festival near the Space Needle that draws hundreds of food vendors, retailers, and performers. Three people were killed — including one suspected gunman — and four others were hospitalised. Among the wounded was a 2-year-old boy.

https://x.com/Newsforce/status/2083227818423423040

Dozens of officers were on scene. According to court documents, at least one officer witnessed a 15-year-old suspect firing into the crowd and quickly persuaded him to surrender. Police say they are still searching for at least one additional person involved in the shooting.

But the department's public response drew sharp rebuke. A full five hours elapsed between the initial social-media post acknowledging the incident and the first press conference, during which residents were left unsure whether an active threat remained. Assistant Chief Tyrone Davis led that briefing; Barnes did not attend.

Barnes Under Pressure

Barnes was in Dallas attending the National Organization of Black Law Enforcement Executives conference when the shooting unfolded. He returned to Seattle for a Monday-morning press conference alongside Mayor Wilson, but the damage to his credibility was already accumulating.

After that briefing, video captured a tense confrontation between Barnes and a reporter who pressed him about his frequent weekend absences from the city — Barnes maintains a family home in Chicago.

"Those reports are wrong, do you understand?"

— Shon Barnes, then-Seattle Police Chief, to a reporter

By Wednesday evening, Barnes appeared at a silent vigil for the shooting victims but left abruptly. Sources told local media he was summoned to a meeting with Mayor Wilson immediately afterward and asked to resign. He began texting associates about his dismissal that night, according to FOX 13 Seattle.

On Thursday afternoon, Barnes issued a measured farewell. "The men and women of this department show up every single day with professionalism and dedication, and what they did in the aftermath of the Bite of Seattle tragedy reflects the very best of who they are," he said. "I hope this transition gives the city and this department the opportunity to return full focus to what matters most — addressing youth gun violence and preventing more tragedies."

Community Divided

Wilson, a democratic socialist who once called for defunding the police, credited officers for a rapid tactical response that likely saved lives but acknowledged the communication failures were unacceptable.

"The courage and professionalism that the officers of the Seattle Police Department showed deserves to be honored. I share Chief Barnes' hope that we can return our focus to addressing youth gun violence and ensuring that every family can feel safe."

— Katie Wilson, Mayor of Seattle

Not everyone backed the move. Black community leaders — including the Seattle branch of the NAACP and the Urban League of Metropolitan Seattle — organised a rally at City Hall on Thursday morning to protest what they characterised as a politically motivated ouster of the city's Black police chief. Barnes had served in the role since late 2024 and was retained by Wilson after she won the mayoral race.

What Comes Next

Deputy Chief Andre Sayles, who has more than 20 years of law-enforcement experience, takes the helm immediately. Wilson is scheduled to formally introduce him at a press conference on Friday at 11 a.m. Pacific and outline the process for selecting a permanent chief.

The criminal investigation into the shooting continues. One teenage suspect is in custody, but police are still searching for at least one other individual involved. The case has intensified a national conversation about youth gun violence and security at large public events — a concern that resonates across immigrant communities, including Indian Americans in the Seattle metropolitan area, who frequent the city's diverse festival circuit.

For the roughly 150,000-strong Indian-American population in the greater Seattle area — one of the largest in the country — the episode underscores questions about public safety at the large community gatherings and cultural festivals that are a staple of diaspora life in the Pacific Northwest.
